JUSTICE VIJAY BISHNOI Judgment / Order 19/04/2017 The matter comes up for consideration of application preferred on behalf of the State seeking condonation of delay of 672 days in filing this leave to appeal.

Learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that inadvertently the State has filed an appeal against the judgment dated 31.10.2013 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hanumangarh (for short 'the trial court' hereinafter) in Cr. Regular Case No.212/2005, whereby the trial court has acquitted the accused-respondents from the offence punishable under section (2 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] 7/16 (1)
a (i) of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short 'the Act of 1954' hereinafter) before the Court of Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities Cases), Hanumangarh (for short 'the appellate court'
hereinafter), however, the said appeal was dismissed by the appellate court vide judgment dated 04.12.2014 as not maintainable.

entities.text: Court of Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities Cases), Hanumangarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, the State has now preferred this leave to appeal before this Court.

Learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that the delay in filing this leave to appeal is bonafide and,
therefore, the same deserves to be condoned.

1

Per contra, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents Mr M.S.Singhvi assisted by Mr Angadh Mirdha & Mr Deepak Chandak has vehemently opposed the application seeking condonation of delay in filing this leave to appeal and argued that the State has failed to explain the delay in filing this leave to appeal sufficiently, hence, the delay is not liable to be condoned.

After hearing learned counsels for the parties and after going through the averments made in the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the same is allowed and the delay in filing this leave to appeal is condoned.
With the consent of learned counsels for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

The present leave to appeal is filed by the State seeking leave to file appeal against the judgment dated 31.10.2013 passed by the trial court in Cr. Regular Case No.212/2005, whereby the trial court has acquitted the accused- (3 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] respondents from the offence punishable under section 7/16 (1) a (i) of the Act of 1954.

Brief facts of the case are that PW.1 Raghunath Singh filed a complaint before the trial court on 01.04.2005 alleging therein that he was posted as Food Inspector in the Office of Chief Medical and Health Officer, Hanumangarh on 26.03.2004 and on that day at about 6:00 P.M., he inspected Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal situated at Dhan Mandi, Goluwala.

entities.text: Office of Chief Medical and Health Officer, Hanumangarh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: At that time, Kundan Lal son of Ishardas Arora was present as the owner of the firm and was selling the food items.

After introducing himself, he inspected the refined mustard oil (Bansri Brand) and on suspicion of adulteration, he purchased three one litre packets of said refined mustard oil and paid Rs.183/- to Kundanlal.
The samples of said mustard oil were sent for chemical examination and from the report thereof, it was found that it was adulterated.

A complaint for commission of offence under section 7/16 of the Act of 1954 was filed against the proprietor Kundanlal, Chhaganlal and Mukul Kishore, wherein, it was alleged that Kundanlal and Chhaganlal are the partners of Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal, whereas the accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the nominee of the company, which had manufactured the said adulterated mustard oil.
The trial court after taking cognizance against the accused-respondents had framed charges for the aforesaid offence against them.
It is noticed that during the course of trial, one of the accused-respondent Kundanlal died and,
therefore, the trial (4 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] against him was dropped.
To prove its case, the prosecution had produced three witnesses and also got exhibited as many as 30 documents.
The statements of the accused-respondents were recorded under section 313 CrPC and in defence, DW.1 Dr. Prem Kumar was produced.

State vs Chaggan Lal & Anr on 19 April, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86704250/
2

The trial court after pondering over the evidence adduced by the prosecution and the defence has acquitted the accused-respondents from the offence punishable under section 7/16 (1) a (i) of the Act of 1954 vide impugned judgment dated 31.10.2013 while holding that the prosecution has failed to prove the fact that the accused-Chhaganlal was partner of Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal on the day when the Food Inspector had inspected the said firm and collected the samples of mustard oil,
which were later on found to be adulterated.

So far as accused-respondent Mukul Kishore is concerned, the trial court has held that the prosecution has failed to prove that Mukul Kishore was the nominee of the Firm Amrit Enterprises,
which had manufactured the mustard oil, which was found to be adulterated.

Learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that the prosecution has sufficiently proved the fact that the accused- respondent Chhagan Lal was the partner of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal on the day when the inspection of the said firm was carried out by the Food Inspector PW.1 Raghunath Singh and samples of the adulterated mustard oil were collected.

Learned Public Prosecutor has argued that PW.1 Raghunath Singh in his (5 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] statement before the court has specifically stated that accused- respondent Chhagan Lal was one of the partners of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal on 26.03.2004 and to substantiate the same, he also got exhibited a letter Ex.P/17 said to have been issued by the Assistant Commercial Taxation Officer, Hanumangarh dated 09.11.2004.
It is contended that the trial court has not appreciated the said piece of evidence in right perspective.

Learned Public Prosecutor has further argued that by producing Ex.P/18 and Ex.P/19 the prosecution has sufficiently proved that the accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the nominee of the company on 26.03.2004, however, the trial court without appreciating the said piece of evidence has illegally held that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the day when the inspection was carried out by the Food Inspector in the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal, the accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of Amrit Enterprises, which had allegedly manufactured the adulterated mustard oil.

Learned Public Prosecutor has, therefore,
submitted that in view of the evidence produced by the prosecution before the trial court, prima facie it is proved that the trial court has grossly erred in acquitting the accused-respondents.

Hence,
it is a fit case wherein the leave should be granted.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents has argued that since the prosecution has failed to prove that the accused-respondent Chhagan Lal was the partner of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal on 26.03.2004, the trial court has rightly acquitted the accused-respondents from the offence punishable (6 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] under section 7/16 (1) a (i) of the Act of 1954.

It is contended that respondent - Chhagan Lal was partner of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal from 31.05.1977 to 03.09.1995 and from 04.09.1995, the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal was a proprietorship firm to which late Kundan Lal was the sole proprietor.
It is also contended that from Ex.P/6, From VI produced along with the complaint, it is clear that late Kundan Lal was the proprietor of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal.

Learned counsel for the respondents has invited the attention of this Court towards Ex.D/1, a certificate issued by the Assistant Commercial Taxation Officer, Hanumangarh on 20.09.2005,
wherein it is certified that Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal was a partnership firm from 31.05.1977 to State vs Chaggan Lal & Anr on 19 April, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86704250/
3 03.09.1995 and thereafter the said firm became the proprietorship firm of which late Kundan Lal was the proprietor.

Learned counsel for the respondent has, therefore, submitted that from the above fact, it is clear that on the day i.e. 26.03.2004 when the Food Inspector inspected the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal and collected samples of the refined mustard oil, the respondent Chhagan Lal was not the partner of the firm.

Learned counsel for the respondents has further argued that the prosecution has failed to produce cogent and reliable evidence to prove that on 26.03.2004, respondent - Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of the Amrit Enterprises, who had allegedly manufactured the adulterated mustard oil.

Learned counsel for the respondents has also argued that the prosecution has failed to prove that Ex.P/18 and Ex.P/19 were issued by the (7 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] authorized signatory of the Amrit Enterprises or the Local Health Authority of Abohar (Punjab), where the Amrit Enterprises is situated.
It is contended that Ex.P/18 and Ex.P/19 have not been proved by the prosecution by producing any witness regarding the issuance of the said documents.

Learned counsel for the respondents has, therefore, submitted that the trial court has rightly held that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the day i.e. 26.03.2004 when the Food Inspector inspected the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal at Goluwala and collected the samples of adulterated mustard oil,
respondent- Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of the Amrit Enterprises, which had manufactured the said mustard oil.

Learned counsel for the respondents has, therefore, prayed that in view of the above facts and circumstances of the case, no case for grant of leave is made out,
hence, the leave to appeal to this Court is liable to be rejected.
Heard learned counsels for the rival parties and carefully scrutinized the record of the case.

The prosecution against the accused-respondents was launched with the allegation that when the samples of adulterated mustard oil was collected from the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal at Goluwala on 26.03.2004, the accused-respondent Chhagan Lal was the partner of the said firm and the accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of the Amrit Enterprises, which had manufactured the said adulterated mustard oil.

To prove the fact that accused-respondent Chhagan Lal (8 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] was the partner of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal on 26.03.2004, the prosecution has produced Ex.P/17, a letter dated 09.11.2004 said to have been issued by the Assistant Commercial Taxation Officer,
Hanumangarh, however, the prosecution witness PW.1 Raghunath Singh in his statement recorded before the trial court has categorically admitted that on the day of inspection only late Kundan Lal was present at the firm and Chhagan Lal was not there.
He has also admitted that in Ex.P/12 Kundan Lal was shown as the proprietor of the firm.

Apart from that, Ex.D/1 produced on behalf of the accused-respondents issued by the Assistant Commercial Taxation Officer on 20.09.2005 clearly states that accused-respondent Chhagan Lal was the partner of the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal up to 03.09.1995 and thereafter, the said firm is a proprietorship firm of which late Kundan Lal was the sole proprietor.
State vs Chaggan Lal & Anr on 19 April, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86704250/

4 To prove the allegation that accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of Amrit Enterprises, which had allegedly manufactured the adulterated mustard oil, the prosecution has produced Ex.P/18 and Ex.P/19 said to have been issued by the authorized signatory of Amrit Enterprises or the Local Health Authority, Abohar (Punjab) respectively.
However, PW.1 Raghunath in his statement has clearly admitted that Ex.P/19 is not signed by anybody and it is simply attested by a Notary of Hanumangarh.
He has also admitted that he did not collect any information regarding issuance of Ex.P/19 from the Medical Department of Abohar.

PW.1 Raghunath Singh has also failed to explain that from whom he had received Ex.P/18, the (9 of 9) [CRLLA-385/2015] letter declaring accused-respondent Mukul Kishore as authorized nominee of Amrit Enterprises.

After hearing learned counsels for the parties and after carefully scrutinizing the record, this Court is of the opinion that the prosecution has failed to prove before the trial court that at the time when the Food Inspector PW.1 Raghunath Singh inspected the Firm Kundan Lal Chhagan Lal at Goluwala on 26.03.2004 and collected samples of adulterated mustard oil, the accused-respondent Chhagan Lal was the partner of the said firm and the accused-respondent Mukul Kishore was the authorized nominee of Amrit Enterprises, which had allegedly manufactured the said adulterated mustard oil.

In view of the above discussions, this Court is of the opinion that the trial court has not committed any illegality in acquitting the accused-respondents from the offence punishable under section 7/16 (1) a (i) of the Act of 1954 vide impugned judgment.
Consequently, this leave to appeal is rejected.

(VIJAY BISHNOI)J. m.asif/PS State vs Chaggan Lal & Anr on 19 April, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86704250/
